data.narrative:
Cylib, a Series A Climate & Energy company founded by Lilian Schwich, Gideon Schwich, and Paul Sabarny, has raised €140M+ in combined equity and grant capital (€55M Series A, €26.1M NRW grant, €63.4M BMWE grant). The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises nine private peers—including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen—plus one public comparable (LNZA).

Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x multiplier to the €140M capital raised proxy, a standard step-up assumption for Series A advancement. This method yields an implied valuation of €280M. A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Climate & Energy segment; filtering across valuation tier and stage yielded fewer than three datapoints, making sector-wide median aggregation unreliable.

The triangulated valuation range is €238M (low) to €322M (high), with a median of €280M. Given reliance on a single methodological input, material uncertainty surrounds the appropriate step-up multiplier and the degree to which grant capital should be weighted alongside equity. Key risks include technology maturity, capital intensity of deployment, and regulatory/subsidy policy shifts in the climate-tech landscape. Investors should supplement this stage-based framework with deeper diligence on unit economics, deployment timeline, and grant-funding stability.
